observation_summary: The methods appendFixedWidthPadLeft and appendFixedWidthPadRight in StrBuilder throw a NullPointerException when appending a null object if the null text has not been configured.
reasoning_summary: The code attempts to call .length() on the result of getNullText() without verifying if that result is null. This is a classic missing guard/validation issue. While the fix might involve handling the null result, the root cause is the lack of a check on the return value of getNullText() before invoking a method on it.
evidence_used: StrBuilder.java:1185: String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
StrBuilder.java:1229: String str = (obj == null ? getNullText() : obj.toString());
Bug report description: Appending a null value with fixed width causes a null pointer exception if getNullText() has not been set.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The issue is not that the variable is initialized to the wrong value, but that the code fails to validate the state of the object (null) before proceeding with operations.
The procedural logic for padding is correct; the failure is due to a missing safety check on the input data.
